scplotter to work with 10x Visium data prepared by Giotto¶

The technology. 10x Genomics Visium captures whole-transcriptome gene expression from a tissue section on barcoded spots roughly 55 um across, so each spot mixes one to a handful of cells. The section is H&E stained before capture, which is why Visium data can be drawn either on the spot coordinates alone or on top of the histology image. Being sequencing-based, Visium is unbiased in which genes it measures, but it trades single-cell resolution for breadth.

What this notebook covers. Building a Giotto object from a Visium folder, quality filtering and normalisation, highly-variable feature selection, PCA/UMAP embedding, Leiden clustering on a spatial Delaunay network, and then the scplotter views that matter for spot data: SpatDimPlot with and without the tissue image, FeatureStatPlot for marker genes, and CellStatPlot for cluster composition.

Data. 10x mouse brain (sagittal), the same section used in the Giotto workshop sessions Visium parts I and II.

Before you run. Giotto needs a Python environment for its Leiden/UMAP calls — point GIOTTO_PYTHON at it and install scplotter with devtools::load_all() as the setup cell does.

Upstream tutorial.

  • https://giotto-suite.github.io/giotto_workshop_2024/visium-part-i.html
  • https://giotto-suite.github.io/giotto_workshop_2024/visium-part-ii.html

Go back to scplotter documentation: https://pwwang.github.io/scplotter/

library(Giotto)

# Ensure Giotto can access a python env
genv_exists <- suppressMessages(checkGiottoEnvironment())
print(genv_exists)

python_path <- Sys.getenv("GIOTTO_PYTHON")
Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = python_path)

invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(set_giotto_python_path(python_path = python_path))))

In [2]:
library(Giotto)

## Set instructions
results_folder <- "data/Adult_Mouse_Brain.results"

instructions <- createGiottoInstructions(
    save_dir = results_folder,
    save_plot = FALSE,
    show_plot = TRUE,
    return_plot = TRUE,
    python_path = python_path
)

## Provide the path to the visium folder
data_path <- "data/Adult_Mouse_Brain"

## Create object directly from the visium folder
visium_brain <- createGiottoVisiumObject(
    visium_dir = data_path,
    expr_data = "raw",
    png_name = "tissue_lowres_image.png",
    gene_column_index = 2,
    instructions = instructions
)

visium_brain$in_tissue <- ifelse(visium_brain$in_tissue == 1, "Yes", "No")
# visium_brain@cell_metadata

metadata <- getCellMetadata(gobject = visium_brain,
                            output = "data.table")

in_tissue_barcodes <- metadata[in_tissue == "Yes"]$cell_ID

visium_brain <- subsetGiotto(gobject = visium_brain,
                             cell_ids = in_tissue_barcodes)

visium_brain_statistics <- addStatistics(gobject = visium_brain,
                                         expression_values = "raw")

In [6]:
visium_brain <- filterGiotto(
    gobject = visium_brain,
    expression_threshold = 1,
    feat_det_in_min_cells = 50,
    min_det_feats_per_cell = 1000,
    expression_values = "raw",
    verbose = TRUE
)

visium_brain <- normalizeGiotto(
    gobject = visium_brain,
    scalefactor = 6000,
    verbose = TRUE
)

visium_brain <- addStatistics(gobject = visium_brain)

In [9]:
visium_brain <- runPCA(gobject = visium_brain)
my_features <- head(getFeatureMetadata(visium_brain,
                                       output = "data.table")$feat_ID,
                                       1000)
visium_brain <- runPCA(gobject = visium_brain,
                       feats_to_use = my_features,
                       name = "custom_pca")
visium_brain <- runUMAP(visium_brain,
                        dimensions_to_use = 1:10)
visium_brain <- runtSNE(gobject = visium_brain,
                        dimensions_to_use = 1:10)
visium_brain <- createNearestNetwork(gobject = visium_brain,
                                     dimensions_to_use = 1:10,
                                     k = 15)
visium_brain <- createNearestNetwork(gobject = visium_brain,
                                     dimensions_to_use = 1:10,
                                     k = 15,
                                     type = "kNN")
visium_brain <- doLeidenCluster(gobject = visium_brain,
                                resolution = 0.4,
                                n_iterations = 1000)
visium_brain <- doLouvainCluster(visium_brain)

visium_brain@cell_metadata$cell$rna$leiden_clus <- as.factor(visium_brain@cell_metadata$cell$rna$leiden_clus)
visium_brain@cell_metadata$cell$rna$louvain_clus <- as.factor(visium_brain@cell_metadata$cell$rna$louvain_clus)
